newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany holds suspected discotheque bombers.
newsitem.headline: Germany holds suspected discotheque bombers.

text.p: German justice officials said on Friday they had arrested two people suspected of a central role in the bombing of a West Berlin nightclub ten years ago which killed three and wounded 200, including many U.S. servicemen.

The United States blamed Libya for the attack on the "La Belle" nightclub and responded by bombing Tripoli, killing at least 15 people, including an adopted 15-month-old daughter of leader Muammar Gaddafi and wounding more than 100.

The Berlin authorities said they had arrested a 37-year old woman, identified only as Verena C., and her former husband, Ali C., on Thursday. They said they suspected she planted the bomb at the request of Ali C. and another suspect, Yasser Shraydi.
Shraydi was extradited to Germany from Lebanon in May this year.

The justice officials said they had also issued arrest warrants for three former members of the Libyan embassy in East Berlin -- identified only by the surnames Elamin, Keshlaf and Al Abani -- and a Libyan secret service member named Rashed.
They were suspected of having initiated the attack and providing the explosives and were presumably back in Libya now, the Berlin authorities' statement said.
Two U.S. soldiers and a woman were killed on the attack on the disco in Berlin's Schoeneberg district and scores of off-duty U.S. military personnel were injured.
Prosecutors' investigations into the bombing suffered a setback earlier this year when one of the key witnesses died in a car crash in Portugal.
Rainer Wiegand, a former official of the East German Stasi intelligence service, and his wife died on June 17 when their rented car was involved in a head-on collision in the south of the country.
Press reports said Wiegand had provided investigators with Stasi information on Arab guerrillas after German unification in 1990. Prosecutors have declined to comment on the reports.
